The overview

Mexico City is a high-altitude megacity of world-class museums, leafy plazas and one of the planet's great food scenes, layered over an ancient Aztec capital.

Top things to do in Mexico City

  • Walk the Zocalo and Templo Mayor
  • See Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul
  • Float the canals of Xochimilco
  • Visit the Teotihuacan pyramids
  • Eat tacos al pastor across Roma and Condesa

Best time to visit

The sweet spot for Mexico City is generally Mar–May (dry) — and the cheapest fares often land just outside peak season.

Is it safe?

Use caution; varies by region. Watch your belongings in crowds and tourist areas, and check your government’s current advisory before you go. Visa for US passports: Visa-free, up to 180 days.

A bit of history

Built on the Aztec island-capital of Tenochtitlan (founded 1325), it became the heart of New Spain after 1521 and today is the largest city in North America.

Culture & language

Mexican culture is vibrant and deeply traditional — Day of the Dead, mariachi, muralism, and a profound culinary heritage recognized by UNESCO.

Language: Spanish · English spoken: Common in tourist areas
